data.narrative: Devanshi demonstrated exceptional competence in technical task specification and AI-ready ticket authoring. Decomposed two vertical slices into 5 atomic, self-contained execution tickets equipped with all 7 core architectural sections. Successfully navigated the 'technically correct disaster' simulation by differentiating cross-cutting standards (centralized exception filters and rate limiting) from ticket-level security contracts (strict session identity binding, idempotency keys, and payload sanitization).

dimension_scores.observation: Authored tickets with zero ambiguity, explicit JSON schemas, exhaustive HTTP status codes, and deterministic Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
Preserved vertical slice requirements flawlessly while isolating concerns across data seeding, provider listings, slot availability, and booking mutations.
Mapped explicit input/output contracts connecting tickets (e.g. TICK-101 seed data IDs consumed by TICK-102 and TICK-103 endpoints).
Identified subtle concurrency risks (double booking race conditions) and mandated atomic conditional update queries in TICK-104.
Quickly diagnosed AI agent roleplay questions, discerning spec gaps from executor autonomy, and hardened TICK-104 against unstated assumptions.
Properly partitioned responsibilities between centralized application middleware (error sanitization, rate limiting) and localized ticket contracts (caller tenancy binding).

strengths: Zero-ambiguity interface contracts with full JSON schemas and error codes
Behavioral Given/When/Then acceptance criteria defining preconditions explicitly
Sharp architectural judgment separating cross-cutting framework filters from ticket-level trust boundaries
